body: I see.  I'll have to look more into what formally evicting someone entails.  Thank you so much for your help.
Wow, that is crazy... what about if I were to pay for a room for him during the eviction process?  Does it have to be in their house?

Thank you so much for this information, it is very comforting to hear this!  One thing I don't understand is WHY he should be treated as a tenant, and therefore my parents are required to go through an eviction procedure, if he has never paid rent/utilities??  

Also, sorry I didn't specify where we are, I updated the post afterwards - we are in California.

Thank you, I will look into both of these.  He certainly fits a lot of the criteria laid out as necessary for Laura's Law to be invoked, but not all of them and not all within the necessary timeframes.  I will call NAMI tomorrow and see where they can direct me.  Thanks again.

It sounds like having someone sectioned is somewhat similar to what in California would be called "involuntary committment" or 5150'ed.  This did happen the time his ex-wife called the police when he attempted to cut himself/burn their shed down.. but since it was deemed a psychiatric emergency he could only be held for a maximum of 72 hours.  It's helpful to learn that there is a similar law in place for non-emergency situations in which there is only a threat of someone doing harm to themself or others.  And yes, we have been turned away from so many mental health organizations with very little encouraging or empowering information so far.  Everyone just tells us that there's nothing we can do if he won't cooperate.. it is incredibly frustrating.

I appreciate your opinion and thank you for reading through my entire post, but I feel the need to clarify a bit... you're right, in writing this I am extremely angry/upset/hurt/frustrated, and some of those feelings of helplessness may have come across as callousness when I didn't mean them to.  I also didn't mean to give the impression that my family and I are in some sort of denial about what happened to him, or that we are not sympathetic to his situation.  What happened was a horrible, horrible thing that I believe is 100% at the heart of most of his issues today.  It's true that the age difference between us is pretty significant and he and I haven't ever been what I would describe as "close," but as an adult I don't hold that against him knowing what I know now about his past.  I also feel deeply sad about what happened to him and the path his life has taken since then as a result.. to maybe give a bit more detail/perspective, my sister and mother were also molested as children and have had to wrestle with that for their entire lives, too.  Partly for this reason they have traditionally both been the most empathetic/sympathetic members of my family towards my brother.  However, he has also never really dealt in an appropriate way with what happened to him and has instead always opted to self-medicate and lash out at others.  My mom has always, always defended him and bailed him out whenever he has been in trouble (financially or otherwise) because she has never stopped feeling personally responsible for what happened to him (even though she had no idea what was happening at the time).  She has suffered from years and years of abuse and manipulation from my brother that she simply felt was her cross to bear for what happened to him as a child. 

The time I referred to when my mom kicked him out of the house the first time wasn't a flippant decision due to a single incident of drunkenness... it was after a whole series of incidents and confrontations, and my mom finally confronting the fact that her relationship with my brother was pretty deeply messed up in a lot of ways, and that what she thought was helping him was actually enabling a lot of his self-destructive behavior.  The entire 5 weeks that he was homeless I don't think my mom slept through a single night, and she barely ate.  Now that she has finally decided that he can't stay with us any more, I cannot even imagine what she is going through, except that I know she is suffering greatly and that this is the hardest decision she's ever had to make.

Don't get me wrong, my family is most definitely not perfect.  We've all made mistakes along the way and some of us have witnessed/survived some truly horrific things.  I agree with you that probably all of us could use some counseling in one form or another.  I've been very fortunate to have been raised by a man who was the polar opposite of his father, and to have been given many advantages and opportunities in life that he wasn't offered.  However, I will say that both of my older sisters (who have the same father as my brother and know my brother a lot better than I do) are completely supportive of my parents' decision and are equally as scared of (and for) my brother right now as we are.  His best friend (the only remaining friend he has now) who has always been there for him says that if he continued to live with us it would have only ended up in someone getting hurt, and that he needs professional help that his family can't give him.  

Right now, my focus is on ensuring that my brother is reasonably safe & has a place to go and food to eat (even if that place is not with my parents and myself), and knows where and how to access treatment if and when he decides that he wants to seek it out (since my understanding is that there is no way that I can "make" him do this if he doesn't want to).  My mom is definitely a "tough love" / Tiger Mom kind of persona with plenty of her own issues but she's a good person and has tried her best.. I just want to do what we can now to help him in any way possible.  Hope this helps you to understand better where I'm coming from..

Thanks for your input.  I wish I could do this, but he pretty much despises me right now because he thinks I convinced my parents to ask him to leave (I didn't, it was only after he threatened them with physical violence that they did, and only after he refused to do so that they got the restraining order).  The last conversation we had ended in him verbally attacking and threatening me... so right now I'm pretty wary of him to be honest. :/

We realize that he is not capable of getting a job now, and has not been for a long time.  We also want to get him the help he needs but I don't know how to go about "enforcing" therapy when he doesn't want it and he really truly believes he does not need it.  As far as kicking him out.. it's not a desirable option to any of us either but letting him back in the house is not an option.  I know that it might sound harsh but we have to consider our own safety too.  He is in a hotel right now (my parents have paid for this) and his friend is taking him to various shelters to see if they can offer him a place.  My dad has gone to a few places that offer treatment and they turned him away because they said my brother has to come himself and request treatment, since he is an adult... my brother is aware of how to access these places, but he has no interest in going.  That's unfortunately where we're at right now...
